chunk_findings.detail: `_scoped` is handed `forced` and threads it all the way into `_covered_by_ci`, but `forced` is only forwarded to `record_measured`; it never suppresses the coverage short-circuit. Given a run where the operator explicitly forces the gate (the flag the caller logs as `gate.started {"forced": True}` and the same flag that `_refuse_repeated_failure` exists to let you override), the code still takes `scope.scope == "covered"`, records `unit_tests` as `"passed"` via `R.record_measured(..., forced=forced)`, and returns `O.ok("gate.run", outcome="passed", ...)` without executing a single test. So `--force` on the unit-tests gate returns a synthetic pass, and the evidence it writes even carries `forced=True` while nothing ran — the one case where the caller's intent is unambiguously "run it anyway". Note also that `tree_sha` is written into the evidence but never compared against the tree the covering `ci` run happened on, so this pass is attributed to the current tree purely by assertion.

chunk_findings.detail: For an item whose `ci` gate ran the reverse-import-closure selection (the subset the affected-tests machinery computes) and passed, the unit-tests gate no longer runs at all: `_scoped` sees `scope.scope == "covered"` and `_covered_by_ci` records the gate as `"passed"`. That is a gate outcome produced by a subset run rather than by the gate itself — precisely the partial outcome for affected-tests that the recorded decision forbids ("builds the import-graph closure only, no partial outcome"). The evidence (`scope.evidence()`, `note: "covered by ..."`) documents the subset, but the gate status consumers read is a plain pass, so any caller inspecting `unit_tests` cannot tell that only the closure ran (and, per the `forced` issue above, may see a pass even when it asked for the full run).

chunk_findings.detail: The new branch makes the *ci gate itself* run on a subset of the suite by default (`cfg.ci.tests_scope == "selected"` is the default, so `asked == "selected"` for every item run unless `--full` is passed, and the fallback to full only triggers for the three conditions the intent lists — unmappable file, config/test-helper change, oversized closure). Concretely: an item changes a string-referenced runtime surface the import closure cannot reach (a template, a CLI entry point named in config, a plugin loaded by dotted name). `CS.plan` maps every changed file fine, the closure is small, so no fallback fires; `_execute` runs only the selected tests; if the missed surface is broken, none of the selected tests fail, and `run()` returns `ok` with `scope={"scope": "selected", ...}` in the evidence. The gate outcome recorded for the item is therefore derived from a partial run of the suite rather than the full run — the exact thing the recorded operator decision forbids: "No partial gate outcome for affected-tests: keep D-gate-economy; B-gap-affected-tests builds the import-graph closure only, no partial outcome." [D-gap-affected-tests-no-partial] The closure is allowed to exist as an aid/economy mechanism, but this hunk promotes it into what the ci gate's ok/fail is computed from; recording the scope in the evidence documents the partial run but does not remove the partial outcome. (If the intent is that the newer 2026-10-16 directive supersedes that record, the record should be amended; as written, this change violates it.)

chunk_findings.detail: `budget` is spent twice. `_execute` is given one `budget`, but it passes `timeout_s=budget` to the non-test hooks run and then again to a second, sequential run for the selected tests. Given `[ci].command` that takes ~0.9×budget to pass and a selected suite that takes ~0.9×budget, a single "selected" `ci run` now occupies up to 1.8×budget of wall clock, where before this change the same parameter bounded the entire run. Any consumer that treats `budget` as the deadline for the `ci run` (e.g. a gate/merge-queue wrapper enforcing the same value) will kill the process group mid-tests, so the run reports a timeout with no `selected tests` check instead of the verdict the tests would have produced. The second run should either be given the remaining budget or the budget semantics should be made explicitly per-command.

chunk_findings.detail: `SKIP={scope.skip} {cmd}` is a *shell variable assignment prefix*, so it only applies to the first simple command of `cmd`. `[ci].command` is operator-controlled and is documented in the same hunk as "the operator's own [ci].command, run as they wrote it" — a compound value is entirely legal. With `cmd = "pre-commit run --all-files --hook-stage pre-push && pytest tests/ -m 'not slow or scenarios'"` (the very pre-push stage named in the change's intent), the assignment is consumed only by the `pre-commit` part; the `pytest tests/ ...` after `&&` runs without `SKIP`, i.e. the ~12000-test full suite still runs, and then `_execute` runs the selected tests on top of it and `_result` records `Check("selected tests (N files)")` plus `scope=selected` evidence. The gate then claims a scoped run while the full suite actually ran, polluting the recall data the change is supposed to produce. The skip should be passed through `child_env`/the environment so it applies to the whole command, not textually prefixed.

chunk_findings.detail: The guard that is supposed to force the whole suite for "changes no import closure can reason about" only lists `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `.importlinter` and `pytest.ini`. A change to `tests/conftest.py` (or to a fixture/helper module that pytest loads implicitly rather than something a test module imports) is not caught: `name` is `conftest.py`, it is not in `INFRASTRUCTURE`, and its suffix `.py` is in `KNOWN_SUFFIXES`, so `_infrastructure` returns `""` and `plan` proceeds to `select(...)`. conftest is not an import edge in the reverse-import closure, so the closure is the wrong instrument for it: if the selection comes back non-empty (anything else in the same commit that maps to tests, or a selector that maps a changed `tests/*.py` to its directory), `plan` returns `scope="selected"` and the item's `ci` gate runs only those tests. Concretely, an item that edits `tests/conftest.py` to add/replace an autouse fixture and breaks `tests/other/test_x.py` can be graded on a selection that does not contain `tests/other/test_x.py`, so the gate records `scope: selected` and passes while a full run fails — contradicting the stated recall rule ("every test failing in a full run is in the selection") and the explicitly required fallback "when conftest … / test helpers change". The intent enumerates exactly this trigger; the code's `INFRASTRUCTURE` set implements the pyproject/pre-commit half of that list and omits the conftest/test-helper half.

chunk_findings.detail: `_after_ci` can declare the gate "covered" even though its own selection says it dropped changed files. `select()` returns a `Scope` whose `cut` ("over `max_files`, not run") and `cut_at` ("hubs the import walk did not pass") record changed files whose tests are *not* in `sel.tests`. The sibling `selected` return explicitly forwards `cut=sel.cut, cut_at=sel.cut_at` so the size/clo-sure fallback can be applied, but when `rest` is empty it returns `Scope("covered", …)` and discards both. Input: a changed hub file that exceeds `gates.unit_tests_max_files` (so `sel.cut` is non-empty and that file's tests are absent from `sel.tests`), whose file-level tests are also absent from the ci gate's recorded `done`. Then `sel.tests ⊆ done`, `rest` is empty, and the function reports "every test this change reaches ran in the ci gate" while the hub's tests run in neither the ci gate nor this one; the previous code path surfaces `cut` so the caller can escalate to the full suite.

chunk_findings.detail: `_after_ci` treats `it.gates["ci"].evidence["ci_scope"]` as having run "on this very tree" (per the new dataclass comment) but never verifies that the recorded run corresponds to the current tree: `ran["sha"]` is read on line ~214 only to interpolate it into the reason strings, and no comparison is made against the current revision/base (nor against uncommitted changes). Input: run `ddflow ci run` (records `ci_scope` with the selection of tree A), then edit an implementation file that is already in that selection, then run the unit_tests gate on tree B. `select` recomputes the same `sel.tests` (the edit does not change the closure) and `done` covers it, so `_after_ci` returns `Scope("covered", …)` and no test is executed against tree B — the modified code is shipped with only its pre-edit test result. The recorded `sha` is truncated to 12 chars purely for display, so nothing binds the evidence to the tree it is used for.

chunk_findings.detail: With the knob added here defaulting to `"selected"`, an ordinary `ddflow ci run` for an item no longer reproduces the pre-push stage it exists to mirror: `AR.run(... full=bool(getattr(a, "full", False)))` in `ddflow/surfaces/commands/ci.py` now runs only the reverse-import-closure tests plus the non-test hooks, and when that subset is green the command still returns 0 and prints "ci: passed". Concretely, take a config with the default `ci.tests_scope = "selected"`, an item whose diff touches only `ddflow/surfaces/commands/operations.py`, and one pre-existing test outside the closure that is broken by that file; `ddflow ci run` reports the gate as passed even though the suite the gate is defined to reproduce (the whole pre-push stage) fails, so the recorded gate outcome now covers only part of the checked suite. That is precisely a partial gate outcome for affected-tests, and the recorded decision for `B-gap-affected-tests` requires the closure to be built "only, no partial outcome"; making the default opt-in (`--full`) does not remove the default case, and the fallback conditions (unmappable file, conftest/pyproject/pre-commit/test-helper change, oversize closure) do not fire for the example above. [D-gap-affected-tests-no-partial]

chunk_findings.detail:
The new expected output adds `ci.tests_scope = "selected"` (default: `ddflow ci run` for one item runs "every non-test pre-push hook plus only the tests the change reaches"), but the same transcript still ships two help strings that assert the opposite about the very same command and are now false for the default run:

- `ci.timeout_s`: "Seconds the CI command may run ... Default 3600: the pre-push set includes the whole test suite." With `tests_scope = "selected"` by default, the pre-push set no longer includes the whole test suite for an item, so the stated rationale for the default is wrong.
- `gates.unit_tests_scope`: the unit_tests gate may run "selected" only once the item's `ci` gate "-- the whole suite on the branch merged with the base -- has PASSED". With the new default, an item's `ci` gate has *not* run the whole suite, so this precondition no longer describes what happened.

Concretely: run `ddflow config` on this project (the `source = "default"` layer shown here), and the operator reads, in one and the same output, both "selected (default) runs ... only the tests the change reaches" for `ci` and "the pre-push set includes the whole test suite" for `ci.timeout_s` / "the whole suite on the branch merged with the base" for the ci gate in `gates.unit_tests_scope`. Either the golden transcript was updated for the new knob but not for the help text the knob invalidates (the test's expected output then disagrees with the product), or the shipped help text is now self-contradictory; both are defects of this change. If the intent is that the whole suite can no longer be assumed to have run at the `ci` gate, the stated safety argument for selecting the `unit_tests` gate ("ci passed ⇒ the whole suite passed on this commit") is no longer valid and must be re-worded to point at the merge-queue/cadence/phase-end runs instead.

chunk_findings.detail: The newly recorded help text for `ci.tests_scope` says the ci command "records the scope, the selected count and the cut set in the gate evidence, and runs the whole suite instead when the selector says so (a hub, conftest, pyproject, the pre-commit config, an unknown file type, or no test reaches the change)". The change's own stated intent is that the run falls back to the *full* suite when "the closure **exceeds a size**". The parenthetical is presented as the complete list of escalation triggers and does not contain a size trigger; instead the text says an oversized/truncated selection is handled by recording a *cut set*, i.e. by running fewer tests and still recording an outcome. Taken literally, an item whose changed module is reached by more test files than the selection cap allows passes its ci gate with the reaching tests silently cut, and the intent's recall guarantee ("every test failing in a full run is in the selection") no longer holds for that item — precisely the case the size trigger was specified to cover by escalating to the whole suite. Either the help text documents behavior the change was not supposed to implement, or the escalation-on-size is missing from the documented (and therefore implemented) trigger list.

chunk_findings.detail:
The new knob `ci.tests_scope` (default `selected`) makes the `ci` gate run only the closure-selected tests, and its own doc in this same output says so. But two other entries in this artifact still assert the opposite and were not updated by the change:

- `gates.unit_tests_scope`: "Selected only once the item's `ci` gate -- **the whole suite on the branch merged with the base** -- has PASSED on the clean commit its tree holds now (ci tests the committed HEAD)". With the shipped default, ci for an ordinary small item runs *selected* tests, not the whole suite, so this stated precondition for the unit_tests selection is false. Note that unit_tests then selects from the *same* closure, so on the per-item path nothing runs the tests outside that closure, while the shipped explanation tells the reader (and the agent deciding whether to run `ddflow tests`/the full suite by hand) that the whole suite already passed at ci.
- `ci.timeout_s`: "Default 3600: **the pre-push set includes the whole test suite**", which is the rationale for the timeout and is likewise no longer true for an item's default ci run.

Input demonstrating it: `ddflow config --explain` on a repo with defaults, i.e. exactly the output recorded here — one entry says the ci default runs "only the tests the change reaches", two entries say ci is the whole suite. The change should either update those texts (state that ci runs selected and the full suite is the cadence/queue/phase-end run) or the new knob's doc is wrong about the default. As shipped, an agent reading this output is told full-suite coverage per item exists when the change removed it.

chunk_findings.detail: `_scoped` short-circuits the affected-tests (`unit_tests`) gate before anything runs: as soon as `TSC.unit_tests_scope(...)` reports `scope.scope == "covered"`, `_covered_by_ci` records the gate as `passed` (via `R.record_measured`) and returns `O.ok("gate.run", outcome="passed", ...)` — the gate's command is never executed and no test result is produced. That is a non-run outcome for the affected-tests gate, which the standing operator decision forbids: "keep D-gate-economy; B-gap-affected-tests builds the import-graph closure only, no partial outcome" [D-gap-affected-tests-no-partial]. Concretely: for an item whose changed files land inside the closure, `ddflow ci run` executes the selection; a later `ddflow gate run unit_tests` on that item returns `outcome=passed` with evidence `{"note": "covered by <ci run>", "tree_sha": <current tree>, ...}` even though no unit_tests command was run. The only guard is the import-graph closure, which the intent itself treats as a heuristic ("a recall check on this repo's last 100 merges") — a file the closure fails to map (or any change made after the covering `ci run`) still yields a green affected-tests gate with no execution behind it. Note also that `forced` is threaded in but does not bypass the shortcut: `ddflow gate run unit_tests --force`, i.e. the operator explicitly asking for a re-run, still returns `passed` (with `forced` stamped in the evidence) without running anything.

chunk_findings.detail: The new scope/selection plan is computed into the local `scope` and handed to `_execute`, but the timeout branch that immediately follows still builds a bare `Result("unavailable", command=cmd, sha=sha, reason=...)` with no `scope=scope`, even though `Result.evidence()` now supports (and the intent requires) recording "the scope and the selection reason in the gate evidence". Concrete input: an item run (`for_item=True`, `[ci].tests_scope = "selected"`) whose selected pytest subset exceeds `[ci].timeout_s`; `_execute` returns `p.kind == TIMEOUT`, the code returns before ever attaching `scope`, and the persisted gate evidence therefore cannot distinguish "the selected subset hung" from "the full suite hung" — the exact diagnostic the new field was added for. The non-timeout paths keep the plan (evidence emits `scope`), so the omission is specific to this early return.

chunk_findings.detail:
`INFRASTRUCTURE` covers `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `.importlinter` and `pytest.ini`, but not `conftest.py`, even though the stated intent requires a full-suite fallback "when conftest/pyproject/pre-commit config/test helpers change". A changed `tests/conftest.py` has `name == "conftest.py"`, so `c in INFRASTRUCTURE`/`name in INFRASTRUCTURE` is false and `suffix == ".py"`, which is in `KNOWN_SUFFIXES`; `_infrastructure` therefore returns `""` and `plan()` proceeds to `select()` instead of returning `Plan("full", ...)`.

The usual safety net (`if not paths: return Plan("full", ...)` for "no test reaches the change") only saves this when *nothing* depends on conftest. As soon as one test module imports conftest (e.g. `from conftest import make_client`), the reverse import closure is non-empty, so the run is planned as "selected" with only the importing test file(s). A change to a shared fixture in conftest then runs a handful of files while every other test that consumes that fixture implicitly is excluded, so a regression passes the item's `ci` gate even though the full suite (run per batch) fails — exactly the recall hole the intent says must be closed by falling back to the full suite for conftest. Adding `conftest.py` to `INFRASTRUCTURE` (or making `_infrastructure` return full for any `conftest.py` basename) restores the required behavior.

chunk_findings.detail: The `covered` verdict trusts the recorded `ci_scope` evidence without checking that the run it describes happened on the tree currently being gated. `sha = str(ran.get("sha", ""))[:12]` is read and then only interpolated into the human-readable reason string — it is never compared with the tree/HEAD the gate is about to run against, so nothing in this code establishes the "on this very tree" claim the dataclass comment and the scope reason rely on. Concretely, take commit A where `src/auth.py` changes: `ci run` selects and runs `tests/test_auth.py` and records `ci_scope = {scope: "selected", sha: A, tests: ["tests/test_auth.py"], selected: 1}`. The agent then edits `src/auth.py` again (commit B) and the unit_tests gate runs. `_after_ci` recomputes `sel = select(tree, base, ...)`, which yields `tests/test_auth.py` again, but `done` already contains that path, so `rest` is empty and the gate returns `Scope("covered", ...)` — `tests/test_auth.py` is never executed against B's `src/auth.py`, which is exactly the recall loss the intent's "every test failing in a full run is in the selection" check exists to prevent. The `scope == "full"` branch is worse: it returns `covered` before any recomputation, so a test file added after the recorded full run (or any test whose subject changed since) is never run at all for the item. The safe behaviour when the recorded sha does not match the tree being gated is to fall back to running this gate's own selection (or full); the code has the information to detect that and does not use it.

chunk_findings.detail: The new help text enumerates the conditions under which `selected` silently becomes a full run: "(a hub, conftest, pyproject, the pre-commit config, an unknown file type, or no test reaches the change)". The stated intent requires two further fallbacks that are absent here: a change to test helpers, and a closure that exceeds a size cap. An operator who changes `tests/helpers.py` (or any shared test helper) and reads this help will believe the ci gate runs the selected subset, when the specified behaviour is to run the whole suite; conversely the size guard is invisible, so the reason a run suddenly took the full suite (or, if the guard is not implemented, that it silently stayed narrow) cannot be diagnosed from the documented contract. The list is written as the enumeration of selector fallbacks, so the omission misdescribes the documented behaviour rather than merely being terse.

chunk_findings.detail: The change makes an item's `ci` gate outcome be computed over a subset of the suite: the test asserts that `CI.run(..., for_item=True)` invokes `pre-commit` with `SKIP=tests,scenarios`, runs exactly one direct `pytest` call for `tests/test_mod.py`, and still returns `res.ok` with evidence `{"scope": "selected", "selected": 1, ...}` — i.e. the gate goes green although the remaining ~12000 tests were never executed (the same file also asserts the `unit_tests` gate reports `scope == "covered"` off that reduced run, so no later gate re-runs them). Concretely: with only `pkg/mod.py` modified, a regression that lives in a test the closure does not reach (dynamic/implicit import, fixture-driven coupling, or an unmapped changed file that the selector silently treats as reaching enough) merges on a green `ci` outcome. D-gap-affected-tests-no-partial records the operator's constraint that B-gap-affected-tests "builds the import-graph closure only, no partial outcome" — using the closure to produce the gate's pass/merge outcome for affected tests is exactly the partial-outcome shape that record rules out; if D-test-economy-r2 (2026-10-16) is intended to supersede it, that should be recorded as a decision before the item gate depends on selection, otherwise this is a merge-safety risk [D-gap-affected-tests-no-partial].

chunk_findings.detail: The change gives `[ci].tests_scope` the default `selected`, i.e. the `ci` gate for one item now runs "every non-test pre-push hook plus only the tests the change reaches", and records "the scope, the selected count and the cut set" in its evidence — by design the ci gate no longer runs the whole suite per item (that is deferred to `ddflow ci run --full`, the merge queue batch, the cadence and phase end). But the `gates.unit_tests_scope` entry in the very same emitted explanation was left unchanged and still states the opposite as the *precondition for selecting unit tests*: "'selected' (default) runs only the tests its change reaches … Selected only once the item's `ci` gate -- the whole suite on the branch merged with the base -- has PASSED on the clean commit its tree holds now (ci tests the committed HEAD)". After this change a passing `ci` means only the selected subset passed, so that parenthetical is false and the documented safety argument for the selected unit_tests gate ("the whole suite already ran at HEAD") is gone: e.g. a task touching `ddflow/cli/*.py` takes `ci` (selected, ~dozens of tests) → passed, then takes `unit_tests` (selected, same closure) → passed, and no run for that item ever executes the hundreds of tests outside the closure, even though both knob descriptions tell the reader a full run happened. `ddflow config --explain` therefore emits two mutually contradictory statements about what a passing `ci` gate contains, and any code path justified by "ci == whole suite" now rests on a premise this change removed; the entry needs to say the fallback/full-suite condition (or be reworded to "ci passed") rather than continuing to assert the whole suite ran.

The only guard is the import-graph closure, which the intent itself treats as a heuristic ("a recall check on this repo's last 100 merges") — a file the closure fails to map (or any change made after the covering `ci run`) still yields a green affected-tests gate with no execution behind it. Note also that `forced` is threaded in but does not bypass the shortcut: `ddflow gate run unit_tests --force`, i.e. the operator explicitly asking for a re-run, still returns `passed` (with `forced` stamped in the evidence) without running anything.

chunk_findings.detail: The new scope/selection plan is computed into the local `scope` and handed to `_execute`, but the timeout branch that immediately follows still builds a bare `Result("unavailable", command=cmd, sha=sha, reason=...)` with no `scope=scope`, even though `Result.evidence()` now supports (and the intent requires) recording "the scope and the selection reason in the gate evidence". Concrete input: an item run (`for_item=True`, `[ci].tests_scope = "selected"`) whose selected pytest subset exceeds `[ci].timeout_s`; `_execute` returns `p.kind == TIMEOUT`, the code returns before ever attaching `scope`, and the persisted gate evidence therefore cannot distinguish "the selected subset hung" from "the full suite hung" — the exact diagnostic the new field was added for. The non-timeout paths keep the plan (evidence emits `scope`), so the omission is specific to this early return.

chunk_findings.detail:
`INFRASTRUCTURE` covers `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `.importlinter` and `pytest.ini`, but not `conftest.py`, even though the stated intent requires a full-suite fallback "when conftest/pyproject/pre-commit config/test helpers change". A changed `tests/conftest.py` has `name == "conftest.py"`, so `c in INFRASTRUCTURE`/`name in INFRASTRUCTURE` is false and `suffix == ".py"`, which is in `KNOWN_SUFFIXES`; `_infrastructure` therefore returns `""` and `plan()` proceeds to `select()` instead of returning `Plan("full", ...)`.

The usual safety net (`if not paths: return Plan("full", ...)` for "no test reaches the change") only saves this when *nothing* depends on conftest. As soon as one test module imports conftest (e.g. `from conftest import make_client`), the reverse import closure is non-empty, so the run is planned as "selected" with only the importing test file(s). A change to a shared fixture in conftest then runs a handful of files while every other test that consumes that fixture implicitly is excluded, so a regression passes the item's `ci` gate even though the full suite (run per batch) fails — exactly the recall hole the intent says must be closed by falling back to the full suite for conftest. Adding `conftest.py` to `INFRASTRUCTURE` (or making `_infrastructure` return full for any `conftest.py` basename) restores the required behavior.

chunk_findings.detail: The `covered` verdict trusts the recorded `ci_scope` evidence without checking that the run it describes happened on the tree currently being gated. `sha = str(ran.get("sha", ""))[:12]` is read and then only interpolated into the human-readable reason string — it is never compared with the tree/HEAD the gate is about to run against, so nothing in this code establishes the "on this very tree" claim the dataclass comment and the scope reason rely on. Concretely, take commit A where `src/auth.py` changes: `ci run` selects and runs `tests/test_auth.py` and records `ci_scope = {scope: "selected", sha: A, tests: ["tests/test_auth.py"], selected: 1}`. The agent then edits `src/auth.py` again (commit B) and the unit_tests gate runs. `_after_ci` recomputes `sel = select(tree, base, ...)`, which yields `tests/test_auth.py` again, but `done` already contains that path, so `rest` is empty and the gate returns `Scope("covered", ...)` — `tests/test_auth.py` is never executed against B's `src/auth.py`, which is exactly the recall loss the intent's "every test failing in a full run is in the selection" check exists to prevent. The `scope == "full"` branch is worse: it returns `covered` before any recomputation, so a test file added after the recorded full run (or any test whose subject changed since) is never run at all for the item. The safe behaviour when the recorded sha does not match the tree being gated is to fall back to running this gate's own selection (or full); the code has the information to detect that and does not use it.

chunk_findings.detail: The new help text enumerates the conditions under which `selected` silently becomes a full run: "(a hub, conftest, pyproject, the pre-commit config, an unknown file type, or no test reaches the change)". The stated intent requires two further fallbacks that are absent here: a change to test helpers, and a closure that exceeds a size cap. An operator who changes `tests/helpers.py` (or any shared test helper) and reads this help will believe the ci gate runs the selected subset, when the specified behaviour is to run the whole suite; conversely the size guard is invisible, so the reason a run suddenly took the full suite (or, if the guard is not implemented, that it silently stayed narrow) cannot be diagnosed from the documented contract. The list is written as the enumeration of selector fallbacks, so the omission misdescribes the documented behaviour rather than merely being terse.

chunk_findings.detail: The change makes an item's `ci` gate outcome be computed over a subset of the suite: the test asserts that `CI.run(..., for_item=True)` invokes `pre-commit` with `SKIP=tests,scenarios`, runs exactly one direct `pytest` call for `tests/test_mod.py`, and still returns `res.ok` with evidence `{"scope": "selected", "selected": 1, ...}` — i.e. the gate goes green although the remaining ~12000 tests were never executed (the same file also asserts the `unit_tests` gate reports `scope == "covered"` off that reduced run, so no later gate re-runs them). Concretely: with only `pkg/mod.py` modified, a regression that lives in a test the closure does not reach (dynamic/implicit import, fixture-driven coupling, or an unmapped changed file that the selector silently treats as reaching enough) merges on a green `ci` outcome. D-gap-affected-tests-no-partial records the operator's constraint that B-gap-affected-tests "builds the import-graph closure only, no partial outcome" — using the closure to produce the gate's pass/merge outcome for affected tests is exactly the partial-outcome shape that record rules out; if D-test-economy-r2 (2026-10-16) is intended to supersede it, that should be recorded as a decision before the item gate depends on selection, otherwise this is a merge-safety risk [D-gap-affected-tests-no-partial].

chunk_findings.detail: The change gives `[ci].tests_scope` the default `selected`, i.e. the `ci` gate for one item now runs "every non-test pre-push hook plus only the tests the change reaches", and records "the scope, the selected count and the cut set" in its evidence — by design the ci gate no longer runs the whole suite per item (that is deferred to `ddflow ci run --full`, the merge queue batch, the cadence and phase end). But the `gates.unit_tests_scope` entry in the very same emitted explanation was left unchanged and still states the opposite as the *precondition for selecting unit tests*: "'selected' (default) runs only the tests its change reaches … Selected only once the item's `ci` gate -- the whole suite on the branch merged with the base -- has PASSED on the clean commit its tree holds now (ci tests the committed HEAD)". After this change a passing `ci` means only the selected subset passed, so that parenthetical is false and the documented safety argument for the selected unit_tests gate ("the whole suite already ran at HEAD") is gone: e.g. a task touching `ddflow/cli/*.py` takes `ci` (selected, ~dozens of tests) → passed, then takes `unit_tests` (selected, same closure) → passed, and no run for that item ever executes the hundreds of tests outside the closure, even though both knob descriptions tell the reader a full run happened. `ddflow config --explain` therefore emits two mutually contradictory statements about what a passing `ci` gate contains, and any code path justified by "ci == whole suite" now rests on a premise this change removed; the entry needs to say the fallback/full-suite condition (or be reworded to "ci passed") rather than continuing to assert the whole suite ran.

chunk_findings.detail: The change lets the `ci` gate run only the reverse-import-closure selection and PASS on that subset (the ci gate was previously defined as "the whole suite on the branch merged with the base"; the updated doc now states it may run "its own selection"). That makes the outcome of the gate that certifies the pre-push stage *partial*, which is exactly what the recorded operator decision forbids: "No partial gate outcome for affected-tests: keep D-gate-economy; B-gap-affected-tests builds the import-graph closure only, no partial outcome." [D-gap-affected-tests-no-partial]. Concrete demonstration: on an item whose changed file the closure cannot fully map — e.g. a change to `services/testselect.py`'s own closure/`MAX_HOPS` logic or to a test helper that is reachable only through a path the closure truncates — the fallback list is finite and the recall check covered "this repo's last 100 merges", not this item; with `tests_scope = 'selected'` (the new default) `ddflow ci run` executes ~200 selected tests, records the selection reason and PASSes the `ci` gate, while the excluded tests that this change actually breaks (a failure the full suite would catch) never run, so the item proceeds on a partial result. The decision kept the closure as an input to the affected-test machinery precisely so that a gate PASS still covers the full stage; the closure should not be promoted into the `ci` gate's pass/fail basis.

chunk_findings.detail: The operator's `[ci].command` still gets the entire `budget`, but the tests hook that replaces the skipped `tests,scenarios` hooks now only gets whatever wall-clock time is left, floored at one second. Given a `[ci].timeout_s` that the pre-stage nearly consumes — e.g. `timeout_s = 300` with a lint/type stage that completes at 299.4 s (or at 300.0 s if the process finishes before the kill lands) — the selected tests receive `max(1, 300 - 299) = 1` second, are killed almost immediately, and the gate fails on a tests-hook timeout even though every selected test passes; before this change the tests hook received the full `budget` and the run passed. The failure is also misattributed: the evidence records a tests-hook timeout/unavailable outcome rather than a budget overrun by the pre-stage, so the operator is pushed toward re-running the full suite instead of raising `[ci].timeout_s`. The floor of `1` guarantees the hook is always started (and therefore always killed) once the pre-stage has consumed the budget, so there is no path where an exhausted budget yields a clean "budget exceeded" outcome.

Recording a `covered`/"selected" outcome in the gate evidence is precisely a partial gate outcome for the affected tests, which [D-gap-affected-tests-no-partial] forbids: "B-gap-affected-tests builds the import-graph closure only, no partial outcome." Concretely, given an item whose changed file maps to a closure smaller than the suite, the `ci` gate reports success and the `unit_tests` gate is never run against that closure, so a regression in an unselected test is reported as green — the closure is used to produce a partial pass rather than only to build the mapping.

chunk_findings.detail: The new parenthetical says that when the item's `ci` gate ran under the new default `[ci].tests_scope = "selected"`, the `unit_tests` gate "then runs" *the tests that ci did not take*. ci's selection is the reverse-import closure of the change, so its complement is essentially the whole suite: for a small fix that touches one leaf module, ci selects (say) 20 of the ~12,000 test files and `unit_tests` is then documented to run the other ~11,980 — i.e. every small/bug-fix item runs a full suite per item anyway, which is exactly the per-item full-suite cost D-test-economy-r2 was introduced to remove, and it contradicts this same file's `cadence.integration_tests_every_tasks` doc ("An item's ci and unit_tests gates run only the tests its change reaches (D-test-economy-r2), so this pass, the merge queue's batch run and the phase-end acceptance are where the whole suite runs ..."). If the intent was instead that the gate re-runs only the tests in *this gate's own* selection that ci cut (normally none), the sentence must say so; as written, the documented composition makes the per-item gates cover the whole suite and makes the cadence pass redundant.

chunk_findings.detail: The regenerated `--explain` output describes the ci selection as recording **"the cut set in the gate evidence"**, i.e. the ci run is truncated by the size cap, and it enumerates the full-suite fallbacks as exactly "a hub, conftest, pyproject, the pre-commit config, an unknown file type, or no test reaches the change" — the "the closure exceeds a size" case is absent. Concrete failure: a changed file whose reverse import closure maps to more than `gates.unit_tests_max_files` (100) test files is cut (two-hop importers dropped first) and the ci gate records `passed`; if the regression being introduced is exercised by one of the dropped tests, the item's ci gate is green, the unit_tests gate is entitled to run only the tests ci did not take, and the breakage is not seen until the merge-queue batch or the `cadence.integration_tests_every_tasks` run. The safer behaviour (and the one the intent names) is a fallback to `ci run --full` in the over-size case, so the doc/selection should say so rather than recording a cut set.

chunk_findings.detail: `_scoped` is handed `forced` and threads it all the way into `_covered_by_ci`, but `forced` is only forwarded to `record_measured`; it never suppresses the coverage short-circuit. Given a run where the operator explicitly forces the gate (the flag the caller logs as `gate.started {"forced": True}` and the same flag that `_refuse_repeated_failure` exists to let you override), the code still takes `scope.scope == "covered"`, records `unit_tests` as `"passed"` via `R.record_measured(..., forced=forced)`, and returns `O.ok("gate.run", outcome="passed", ...)` without executing a single test. So `--force` on the unit-tests gate returns a synthetic pass, and the evidence it writes even carries `forced=True` while nothing ran — the one case where the caller's intent is unambiguously "run it anyway". Note also that `tree_sha` is written into the evidence but never compared against the tree the covering `ci` run happened on, so this pass is attributed to the current tree purely by assertion.

chunk_findings.detail: For an item whose `ci` gate ran the reverse-import-closure selection (the subset the affected-tests machinery computes) and passed, the unit-tests gate no longer runs at all: `_scoped` sees `scope.scope == "covered"` and `_covered_by_ci` records the gate as `"passed"`. That is a gate outcome produced by a subset run rather than by the gate itself — precisely the partial outcome for affected-tests that the recorded decision forbids ("builds the import-graph closure only, no partial outcome"). The evidence (`scope.evidence()`, `note: "covered by ..."`) documents the subset, but the gate status consumers read is a plain pass, so any caller inspecting `unit_tests` cannot tell that only the closure ran (and, per the `forced` issue above, may see a pass even when it asked for the full run).

chunk_findings.detail: The new branch makes the *ci gate itself* run on a subset of the suite by default (`cfg.ci.tests_scope == "selected"` is the default, so `asked == "selected"` for every item run unless `--full` is passed, and the fallback to full only triggers for the three conditions the intent lists — unmappable file, config/test-helper change, oversized closure). Concretely: an item changes a string-referenced runtime surface the import closure cannot reach (a template, a CLI entry point named in config, a plugin loaded by dotted name). `CS.plan` maps every changed file fine, the closure is small, so no fallback fires; `_execute` runs only the selected tests; if the missed surface is broken, none of the selected tests fail, and `run()` returns `ok` with `scope={"scope": "selected", ...}` in the evidence. The gate outcome recorded for the item is therefore derived from a partial run of the suite rather than the full run — the exact thing the recorded operator decision forbids: "No partial gate outcome for affected-tests: keep D-gate-economy; B-gap-affected-tests builds the import-graph closure only, no partial outcome." [D-gap-affected-tests-no-partial] The closure is allowed to exist as an aid/economy mechanism, but this hunk promotes it into what the ci gate's ok/fail is computed from; recording the scope in the evidence documents the partial run but does not remove the partial outcome. (If the intent is that the newer 2026-10-16 directive supersedes that record, the record should be amended; as written, this change violates it.)

chunk_findings.detail: `budget` is spent twice. `_execute` is given one `budget`, but it passes `timeout_s=budget` to the non-test hooks run and then again to a second, sequential run for the selected tests. Given `[ci].command` that takes ~0.9×budget to pass and a selected suite that takes ~0.9×budget, a single "selected" `ci run` now occupies up to 1.8×budget of wall clock, where before this change the same parameter bounded the entire run. Any consumer that treats `budget` as the deadline for the `ci run` (e.g. a gate/merge-queue wrapper enforcing the same value) will kill the process group mid-tests, so the run reports a timeout with no `selected tests` check instead of the verdict the tests would have produced. The second run should either be given the remaining budget or the budget semantics should be made explicitly per-command.

chunk_findings.detail: `SKIP={scope.skip} {cmd}` is a *shell variable assignment prefix*, so it only applies to the first simple command of `cmd`. `[ci].command` is operator-controlled and is documented in the same hunk as "the operator's own [ci].command, run as they wrote it" — a compound value is entirely legal. With `cmd = "pre-commit run --all-files --hook-stage pre-push && pytest tests/ -m 'not slow or scenarios'"` (the very pre-push stage named in the change's intent), the assignment is consumed only by the `pre-commit` part; the `pytest tests/ ...` after `&&` runs without `SKIP`, i.e. the ~12000-test full suite still runs, and then `_execute` runs the selected tests on top of it and `_result` records `Check("selected tests (N files)")` plus `scope=selected` evidence. The gate then claims a scoped run while the full suite actually ran, polluting the recall data the change is supposed to produce. The skip should be passed through `child_env`/the environment so it applies to the whole command, not textually prefixed.

chunk_findings.detail: The guard that is supposed to force the whole suite for "changes no import closure can reason about" only lists `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `.importlinter` and `pytest.ini`. A change to `tests/conftest.py` (or to a fixture/helper module that pytest loads implicitly rather than something a test module imports) is not caught: `name` is `conftest.py`, it is not in `INFRASTRUCTURE`, and its suffix `.py` is in `KNOWN_SUFFIXES`, so `_infrastructure` returns `""` and `plan` proceeds to `select(...)`. conftest is not an import edge in the reverse-import closure, so the closure is the wrong instrument for it: if the selection comes back non-empty (anything else in the same commit that maps to tests, or a selector that maps a changed `tests/*.py` to its directory), `plan` returns `scope="selected"` and the item's `ci` gate runs only those tests. Concretely, an item that edits `tests/conftest.py` to add/replace an autouse fixture and breaks `tests/other/test_x.py` can be graded on a selection that does not contain `tests/other/test_x.py`, so the gate records `scope: selected` and passes while a full run fails — contradicting the stated recall rule ("every test failing in a full run is in the selection") and the explicitly required fallback "when conftest … / test helpers change". The intent enumerates exactly this trigger; the code's `INFRASTRUCTURE` set implements the pyproject/pre-commit half of that list and omits the conftest/test-helper half.

chunk_findings.detail: `_after_ci` can declare the gate "covered" even though its own selection says it dropped changed files. `select()` returns a `Scope` whose `cut` ("over `max_files`, not run") and `cut_at` ("hubs the import walk did not pass") record changed files whose tests are *not* in `sel.tests`. The sibling `selected` return explicitly forwards `cut=sel.cut, cut_at=sel.cut_at` so the size/clo-sure fallback can be applied, but when `rest` is empty it returns `Scope("covered", …)` and discards both. Input: a changed hub file that exceeds `gates.unit_tests_max_files` (so `sel.cut` is non-empty and that file's tests are absent from `sel.tests`), whose file-level tests are also absent from the ci gate's recorded `done`. Then `sel.tests ⊆ done`, `rest` is empty, and the function reports "every test this change reaches ran in the ci gate" while the hub's tests run in neither the ci gate nor this one; the previous code path surfaces `cut` so the caller can escalate to the full suite.

chunk_findings.detail:
The new expected output adds `ci.tests_scope = "selected"` (default: `ddflow ci run` for one item runs "every non-test pre-push hook plus only the tests the change reaches"), but the same transcript still ships two help strings that assert the opposite about the very same command and are now false for the default run:

- `ci.timeout_s`: "Seconds the CI command may run ... Default 3600: the pre-push set includes the whole test suite." With `tests_scope = "selected"` by default, the pre-push set no longer includes the whole test suite for an item, so the stated rationale for the default is wrong.
- `gates.unit_tests_scope`: the unit_tests gate may run "selected" only once the item's `ci` gate "-- the whole suite on the branch merged with the base -- has PASSED". With the new default, an item's `ci` gate has *not* run the whole suite, so this precondition no longer describes what happened.

Concretely: run `ddflow config` on this project (the `source = "default"` layer shown here), and the operator reads, in one and the same output, both "selected (default) runs ... only the tests the change reaches" for `ci` and "the pre-push set includes the whole test suite" for `ci.timeout_s` / "the whole suite on the branch merged with the base" for the ci gate in `gates.unit_tests_scope`. Either the golden transcript was updated for the new knob but not for the help text the knob invalidates (the test's expected output then disagrees with the product), or the shipped help text is now self-contradictory; both are defects of this change. If the intent is that the whole suite can no longer be assumed to have run at the `ci` gate, the stated safety argument for selecting the `unit_tests` gate ("ci passed ⇒ the whole suite passed on this commit") is no longer valid and must be re-worded to point at the merge-queue/cadence/phase-end runs instead.

chunk_findings.detail: The tests hook no longer has its own budget; it gets whatever is left of `budget` after the user's `[ci].command`, clamped to a 1‑second floor. So a slow-but-successful `[ci].command` turns into a spurious gate failure. Concrete input: `[ci].timeout_s = 600` and a `[ci].command` that legitimately takes ~599 s (e.g. the full pre-push stage in a `--full`/integration run, or a slow lint/typecheck step that is not governed by `SKIP`), the tests hook is then invoked with `timeout_s = 1`. The selected tests (or the full suite in `--full` mode) are killed after one second — less than pytest's own interpreter start/collection time — and the gate reports a timeout even though no test failed. Before this diff the tests hook was given the full `budget` (`timeout_s=budget`), so this is a regression that converts "the first command used most of the wall clock" into a hard failure of the item's ci gate. Any `[ci].command` that consumes nearly all of `budget` (the very case the shared-budget scheme is meant to cover) always lands on the 1‑second floor and can never pass, regardless of how fast the selection is.

chunk_findings.detail: `_scoped` short-circuits the affected-tests (`unit_tests`) gate before anything runs: as soon as `TSC.unit_tests_scope(...)` reports `scope.scope == "covered"`, `_covered_by_ci` records the gate as `passed` (via `R.record_measured`) and returns `O.ok("gate.run", outcome="passed", ...)` — the gate's command is never executed and no test result is produced. That is a non-run outcome for the affected-tests gate, which the standing operator decision forbids: "keep D-gate-economy; B-gap-affected-tests builds the import-graph closure only, no partial outcome" [D-gap-affected-tests-no-partial]. Concretely: for an item whose changed files land inside the closure, `ddflow ci run` executes the selection; a later `ddflow gate run unit_tests` on that item returns `outcome=passed` with evidence `{"note": "covered by <ci run>", "tree_sha": <current tree>, ...}` even though no unit_tests command was run. The only guard is the import-graph closure, which the intent itself treats as a heuristic ("a recall check on this repo's last 100 merges") — a file the closure fails to map (or any change made after the covering `ci run`) still yields a green affected-tests gate with no execution behind it. Note also that `forced` is threaded in but does not bypass the shortcut: `ddflow gate run unit_tests --force`, i.e. the operator explicitly asking for a re-run, still returns `passed` (with `forced` stamped in the evidence) without running anything.

chunk_findings.detail: The new scope/selection plan is computed into the local `scope` and handed to `_execute`, but the timeout branch that immediately follows still builds a bare `Result("unavailable", command=cmd, sha=sha, reason=...)` with no `scope=scope`, even though `Result.evidence()` now supports (and the intent requires) recording "the scope and the selection reason in the gate evidence". Concrete input: an item run (`for_item=True`, `[ci].tests_scope = "selected"`) whose selected pytest subset exceeds `[ci].timeout_s`; `_execute` returns `p.kind == TIMEOUT`, the code returns before ever attaching `scope`, and the persisted gate evidence therefore cannot distinguish "the selected subset hung" from "the full suite hung" — the exact diagnostic the new field was added for. The non-timeout paths keep the plan (evidence emits `scope`), so the omission is specific to this early return.

chunk_findings.detail:
`INFRASTRUCTURE` covers `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `.importlinter` and `pytest.ini`, but not `conftest.py`, even though the stated intent requires a full-suite fallback "when conftest/pyproject/pre-commit config/test helpers change". A changed `tests/conftest.py` has `name == "conftest.py"`, so `c in INFRASTRUCTURE`/`name in INFRASTRUCTURE` is false and `suffix == ".py"`, which is in `KNOWN_SUFFIXES`; `_infrastructure` therefore returns `""` and `plan()` proceeds to `select()` instead of returning `Plan("full", ...)`.

The usual safety net (`if not paths: return Plan("full", ...)` for "no test reaches the change") only saves this when *nothing* depends on conftest. As soon as one test module imports conftest (e.g. `from conftest import make_client`), the reverse import closure is non-empty, so the run is planned as "selected" with only the importing test file(s). A change to a shared fixture in conftest then runs a handful of files while every other test that consumes that fixture implicitly is excluded, so a regression passes the item's `ci` gate even though the full suite (run per batch) fails — exactly the recall hole the intent says must be closed by falling back to the full suite for conftest. Adding `conftest.py` to `INFRASTRUCTURE` (or making `_infrastructure` return full for any `conftest.py` basename) restores the required behavior.

chunk_findings.detail: The `covered` verdict trusts the recorded `ci_scope` evidence without checking that the run it describes happened on the tree currently being gated. `sha = str(ran.get("sha", ""))[:12]` is read and then only interpolated into the human-readable reason string — it is never compared with the tree/HEAD the gate is about to run against, so nothing in this code establishes the "on this very tree" claim the dataclass comment and the scope reason rely on. Concretely, take commit A where `src/auth.py` changes: `ci run` selects and runs `tests/test_auth.py` and records `ci_scope = {scope: "selected", sha: A, tests: ["tests/test_auth.py"], selected: 1}`. The agent then edits `src/auth.py` again (commit B) and the unit_tests gate runs. `_after_ci` recomputes `sel = select(tree, base, ...)`, which yields `tests/test_auth.py` again, but `done` already contains that path, so `rest` is empty and the gate returns `Scope("covered", ...)` — `tests/test_auth.py` is never executed against B's `src/auth.py`, which is exactly the recall loss the intent's "every test failing in a full run is in the selection" check exists to prevent. The `scope == "full"` branch is worse: it returns `covered` before any recomputation, so a test file added after the recorded full run (or any test whose subject changed since) is never run at all for the item. The safe behaviour when the recorded sha does not match the tree being gated is to fall back to running this gate's own selection (or full); the code has the information to detect that and does not use it.

chunk_findings.detail: The new help text enumerates the conditions under which `selected` silently becomes a full run: "(a hub, conftest, pyproject, the pre-commit config, an unknown file type, or no test reaches the change)". An operator who changes `tests/helpers.py` (or any shared test helper) and reads this help will believe the ci gate runs the selected subset, when the specified behaviour is to run the whole suite; conversely the size guard is invisible, so the reason a run suddenly took the full suite (or, if the guard is not implemented, that it silently stayed narrow) cannot be diagnosed from the documented contract. Given a `[ci].timeout_s` that the pre-stage nearly consumes — e.g. `timeout_s = 300` with a lint/type stage that completes at 299.4 s (or at 300.0 s if the process finishes before the kill lands) — the selected tests receive `max(1, 300 - 299) = 1` second, are killed almost immediately, and the gate fails on a tests-hook timeout even though every selected test passes; before this change the tests hook received the full `budget` and the run passed. chunk_findings.detail: The new branch makes the *ci gate itself* run on a subset of the suite by default (`cfg.ci.tests_scope == "selected"` is the default, so `asked == "selected"` for every item run unless `--full` is passed, and the fallback to full only triggers for the three conditions the intent lists — unmappable file, config/test-helper change, oversized closure). Concretely: an item changes a string-referenced runtime surface the import closure cannot reach (a template, a CLI entry point named in config, a plugin loaded by dotted name). `CS.plan` maps every changed file fine, the closure is small, so no fallback fires; `_execute` runs only the selected tests; if the missed surface is broken, none of the selected tests fail, and `run()` returns `ok` with `scope={"scope": "selected", ...}` in the evidence. The gate outcome recorded for the item is therefore derived from a partial run of the suite rather than the full run — the exact thing the recorded operator decision forbids: "No partial gate outcome for affected-tests: keep D-gate-economy; B-gap-affected-tests builds the import-graph closure only, no partial outcome." [D-gap-affected-tests-no-partial] The closure is allowed to exist as an aid/economy mechanism, but this hunk promotes it into what the ci gate's ok/fail is computed from; recording the scope in the evidence documents the partial run but does not remove the partial outcome. (If the intent is that the newer 2026-10-16 directive supersedes that record, the record should be amended; as written, this change violates it.)

chunk_findings.detail: `budget` is spent twice. `_execute` is given one `budget`, but it passes `timeout_s=budget` to the non-test hooks run and then again to a second, sequential run for the selected tests. Given `[ci].command` that takes ~0.9×budget to pass and a selected suite that takes ~0.9×budget, a single "selected" `ci run` now occupies up to 1.8×budget of wall clock, where before this change the same parameter bounded the entire run. Any consumer that treats `budget` as the deadline for the `ci run` (e.g. a gate/merge-queue wrapper enforcing the same value) will kill the process group mid-tests, so the run reports a timeout with no `selected tests` check instead of the verdict the tests would have produced. The second run should either be given the remaining budget or the budget semantics should be made explicitly per-command.

chunk_findings.detail: `SKIP={scope.skip} {cmd}` is a *shell variable assignment prefix*, so it only applies to the first simple command of `cmd`. `[ci].command` is operator-controlled and is documented in the same hunk as "the operator's own [ci].command, run as they wrote it" — a compound value is entirely legal. With `cmd = "pre-commit run --all-files --hook-stage pre-push && pytest tests/ -m 'not slow or scenarios'"` (the very pre-push stage named in the change's intent), the assignment is consumed only by the `pre-commit` part; the `pytest tests/ ...` after `&&` runs without `SKIP`, i.e. the ~12000-test full suite still runs, and then `_execute` runs the selected tests on top of it and `_result` records `Check("selected tests (N files)")` plus `scope=selected` evidence. The gate then claims a scoped run while the full suite actually ran, polluting the recall data the change is supposed to produce. The skip should be passed through `child_env`/the environment so it applies to the whole command, not textually prefixed.

chunk_findings.detail: The guard that is supposed to force the whole suite for "changes no import closure can reason about" only lists `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `.importlinter` and `pytest.ini`. A change to `tests/conftest.py` (or to a fixture/helper module that pytest loads implicitly rather than something a test module imports) is not caught: `name` is `conftest.py`, it is not in `INFRASTRUCTURE`, and its suffix `.py` is in `KNOWN_SUFFIXES`, so `_infrastructure` returns `""` and `plan` proceeds to `select(...)`. conftest is not an import edge in the reverse-import closure, so the closure is the wrong instrument for it: if the selection comes back non-empty (anything else in the same commit that maps to tests, or a selector that maps a changed `tests/*.py` to its directory), `plan` returns `scope="selected"` and the item's `ci` gate runs only those tests. Concretely, an item that edits `tests/conftest.py` to add/replace an autouse fixture and breaks `tests/other/test_x.py` can be graded on a selection that does not contain `tests/other/test_x.py`, so the gate records `scope: selected` and passes while a full run fails — contradicting the stated recall rule ("every test failing in a full run is in the selection") and the explicitly required fallback "when conftest … / test helpers change". The intent enumerates exactly this trigger; the code's `INFRASTRUCTURE` set implements the pyproject/pre-commit half of that list and omits the conftest/test-helper half.

chunk_findings.detail: `_after_ci` can declare the gate "covered" even though its own selection says it dropped changed files. `select()` returns a `Scope` whose `cut` ("over `max_files`, not run") and `cut_at` ("hubs the import walk did not pass") record changed files whose tests are *not* in `sel.tests`. The sibling `selected` return explicitly forwards `cut=sel.cut, cut_at=sel.cut_at` so the size/clo-sure fallback can be applied, but when `rest` is empty it returns `Scope("covered", …)` and discards both. Input: a changed hub file that exceeds `gates.unit_tests_max_files` (so `sel.cut` is non-empty and that file's tests are absent from `sel.tests`), whose file-level tests are also absent from the ci gate's recorded `done`. Then `sel.tests ⊆ done`, `rest` is empty, and the function reports "every test this change reaches ran in the ci gate" while the hub's tests run in neither the ci gate nor this one; the previous code path surfaces `cut` so the caller can escalate to the full suite.

chunk_findings.detail: `_after_ci` treats `it.gates["ci"].evidence["ci_scope"]` as having run "on this very tree" (per the new dataclass comment) but never verifies that the recorded run corresponds to the current tree: `ran["sha"]` is read on line ~214 only to interpolate it into the reason strings, and no comparison is made against the current revision/base (nor against uncommitted changes). Input: run `ddflow ci run` (records `ci_scope` with the selection of tree A), then edit an implementation file that is already in that selection, then run the unit_tests gate on tree B. `select` recomputes the same `sel.tests` (the edit does not change the closure) and `done` covers it, so `_after_ci` returns `Scope("covered", …)` and no test is executed against tree B — the modified code is shipped with only its pre-edit test result. The recorded `sha` is truncated to 12 chars purely for display, so nothing binds the evidence to the tree it is used for.

chunk_findings.detail: With the knob added here defaulting to `"selected"`, an ordinary `ddflow ci run` for an item no longer reproduces the pre-push stage it exists to mirror: `AR.run(... full=bool(getattr(a, "full", False)))` in `ddflow/surfaces/commands/ci.py` now runs only the reverse-import-closure tests plus the non-test hooks, and when that subset is green the command still returns 0 and prints "ci: passed". Concretely, take a config with the default `ci.tests_scope = "selected"`, an item whose diff touches only `ddflow/surfaces/commands/operations.py`, and one pre-existing test outside the closure that is broken by that file; `ddflow ci run` reports the gate as passed even though the suite the gate is defined to reproduce (the whole pre-push stage) fails, so the recorded gate outcome now covers only part of the checked suite. That is precisely a partial gate outcome for affected-tests, and the recorded decision for `B-gap-affected-tests` requires the closure to be built "only, no partial outcome"; making the default opt-in (`--full`) does not remove the default case, and the fallback conditions (unmappable file, conftest/pyproject/pre-commit/test-helper change, oversize closure) do not fire for the example above. chunk_findings.detail:
The new expected output adds `ci.tests_scope = "selected"` (default: `ddflow ci run` for one item runs "every non-test pre-push hook plus only the tests the change reaches"), but the same transcript still ships two help strings that assert the opposite about the very same command and are now false for the default run:

- `ci.timeout_s`: "Seconds the CI command may run ... Default 3600: the pre-push set includes the whole test suite." With `tests_scope = "selected"` by default, the pre-push set no longer includes the whole test suite for an item, so the stated rationale for the default is wrong.
- `gates.unit_tests_scope`: the unit_tests gate may run "selected" only once the item's `ci` gate "-- the whole suite on the branch merged with the base -- has PASSED". With the new default, an item's `ci` gate has *not* run the whole suite, so this precondition no longer describes what happened.

Concretely: run `ddflow config` on this project (the `source = "default"` layer shown here), and the operator reads, in one and the same output, both "selected (default) runs ... only the tests the change reaches" for `ci` and "the pre-push set includes the whole test suite" for `ci.timeout_s` / "the whole suite on the branch merged with the base" for the ci gate in `gates.unit_tests_scope`. Either the golden transcript was updated for the new knob but not for the help text the knob invalidates (the test's expected output then disagrees with the product), or the shipped help text is now self-contradictory; both are defects of this change. If the intent is that the whole suite can no longer be assumed to have run at the `ci` gate, the stated safety argument for selecting the `unit_tests` gate ("ci passed ⇒ the whole suite passed on this commit") is no longer valid and must be re-worded to point at the merge-queue/cadence/phase-end runs instead.

chunk_findings.detail: The newly recorded help text for `ci.tests_scope` says the ci command "records the scope, the selected count and the cut set in the gate evidence, and runs the whole suite instead when the selector says so (a hub, conftest, pyproject, the pre-commit config, an unknown file type, or no test reaches the change)". The change's own stated intent is that the run falls back to the *full* suite when "the closure **exceeds a size**". The parenthetical is presented as the complete list of escalation triggers and does not contain a size trigger; instead the text says an oversized/truncated selection is handled by recording a *cut set*, i.e. by running fewer tests and still recording an outcome. Taken literally, an item whose changed module is reached by more test files than the selection cap allows passes its ci gate with the reaching tests silently cut, and the intent's recall guarantee ("every test failing in a full run is in the selection") no longer holds for that item — precisely the case the size trigger was specified to cover by escalating to the whole suite. Either the help text documents behavior the change was not supposed to implement, or the escalation-on-size is missing from the documented (and therefore implemented) trigger list.

chunk_findings.detail:
The new knob `ci.tests_scope` (default `selected`) makes the `ci` gate run only the closure-selected tests, and its own doc in this same output says so. But two other entries in this artifact still assert the opposite and were not updated by the change:

- `gates.unit_tests_scope`: "Selected only once the item's `ci` gate -- **the whole suite on the branch merged with the base** -- has PASSED on the clean commit its tree holds now (ci tests the committed HEAD)". With the shipped default, ci for an ordinary small item runs *selected* tests, not the whole suite, so this stated precondition for the unit_tests selection is false. Note that unit_tests then selects from the *same* closure, so on the per-item path nothing runs the tests outside that closure, while the shipped explanation tells the reader (and the agent deciding whether to run `ddflow tests`/the full suite by hand) that the whole suite already passed at ci.
- `ci.timeout_s`: "Default 3600: **the pre-push set includes the whole test suite**", which is the rationale for the timeout and is likewise no longer true for an item's default ci run.

Input demonstrating it: `ddflow config --explain` on a repo with defaults, i.e. exactly the output recorded here — one entry says the ci default runs "only the tests the change reaches", two entries say ci is the whole suite. The change should either update those texts (state that ci runs selected and the full suite is the cadence/queue/phase-end run) or the new knob's doc is wrong about the default. As shipped, an agent reading this output is told full-suite coverage per item exists when the change removed it.

chunk_findings.detail: The tests hook no longer has its own budget; it gets whatever is left of `budget` after the user's `[ci].command`, clamped to a 1‑second floor. So a slow-but-successful `[ci].command` turns into a spurious gate failure. Concrete input: `[ci].timeout_s = 600` and a `[ci].command` that legitimately takes ~599 s (e.g. the full pre-push stage in a `--full`/integration run, or a slow lint/typecheck step that is not governed by `SKIP`), the tests hook is then invoked with `timeout_s = 1`. The selected tests (or the full suite in `--full` mode) are killed after one second — less than pytest's own interpreter start/collection time — and the gate reports a timeout even though no test failed. Before this diff the tests hook was given the full `budget` (`timeout_s=budget`), so this is a regression that converts "the first command used most of the wall clock" into a hard failure of the item's ci gate. Any `[ci].command` that consumes nearly all of `budget` (the very case the shared-budget scheme is meant to cover) always lands on the 1‑second floor and can never pass, regardless of how fast the selection is.

chunk_findings.detail: The new description for `[ci].tests_scope` says a selected ci run "records the scope, the selected count and the cut set in the gate evidence" — i.e. when the closure is larger than `gates.unit_tests_max_files` (100) the farthest test files are simply dropped and the gate still records a normal PASS on the remainder. That contradicts the requirement this change is supposed to implement: for an oversized closure the run must fall back to the FULL suite (the stated recall guarantee is "every test failing in a full run is in the selection"). Concrete case: a task whose change reaches 150 test files with `gates.unit_tests_max_files = 100`; `ddflow ci run` selects the 100 nearest, records the 50-file cut set, and passes, while the other per-item checks are the same selection — so a failure living in one of the 50 cut files is green in the item's `ci` gate unless the batch merge-queue/cadence run happens to catch it. The fallback list in the same sentence ("a hub, conftest, pyproject, the pre-commit config, an unknown file type, or no test reaches the change") also omits the size case, so nothing in the documented behavior restores full-suite coverage for that input.
